definition: A single thin straight line or smooth curve drawn to follow the trend of plotted points, with the points spread evenly on both sides; it need not pass through every point or through the origin.
Reading a value from a best-fit line at a point between the plotted points, inside the range of the data.
Extending a best-fit line beyond the plotted points, for example back to an axis to find an intercept, to read a value outside the range of the data.
A result that lies well outside the general pattern of the other results: much higher or much lower than expected.
An error that makes repeated readings scatter unpredictably above and below the true value; repeating the readings and taking a mean reduces its effect.
An error that shifts every reading in the same direction, often by the same amount, such as a zero error; repeating the readings does not reduce it.
The doubt in a measurement or a conclusion: how far the true value could be from the result, or how far the conclusion can be trusted.
